Flat Heroes, developed and published by Parallel Circles, is a precision-focused action platformer that demonstrates how a simple concept can evolve into something remarkably engaging through strong design and mechanical depth. On the surface, the game appears minimalistic almost to an extreme. Players control a small square moving through geometric arenas while avoiding hazards and surviving increasingly demanding challenges. However, beneath that stripped-down presentation lies a carefully crafted experience built around movement mastery, fast reactions, and skill progression that rewards patience and persistence.

The game immediately establishes its philosophy through simplicity. There are no elaborate progression trees, complicated mechanics, or overwhelming tutorials. Players receive a compact set of abilities that includes running, jumping, dashing, and attacking. Those basic actions become the foundation for everything that follows. Rather than expanding complexity through additional mechanics, Flat Heroes focuses on pushing players to master the systems already available.

Movement quickly becomes the heart of the experience. Controls feel responsive and reliable, creating an immediate sense of precision that proves essential as challenges become more difficult. Small adjustments in positioning matter. Timing becomes increasingly important. Successful movement through dangerous arenas often feels satisfying because survival depends entirely on execution rather than upgrades or numerical advantages.

The progression structure consistently introduces new ideas without losing focus. Hundreds of handcrafted stages gradually expand the challenge through fresh obstacle combinations and increasingly demanding scenarios. Levels often revolve around survival mechanics where players must avoid projectiles, dangerous environmental hazards, and enemy attacks while maintaining control under pressure. New threats appear regularly enough to prevent repetition while reinforcing core movement skills.

One of the strongest accomplishments Flat Heroes achieves is difficulty balance. Early stages introduce mechanics clearly and provide room for learning before later areas begin demanding significantly greater precision. The game rarely feels unfair because failure usually comes from personal mistakes rather than unpredictable systems. Repeated attempts steadily build familiarity and confidence, turning difficult sections into opportunities for improvement rather than frustration.

The difficulty curve encourages mastery in a rewarding way. Progress often feels earned because success depends directly on developing stronger movement habits and improving reaction speed. Players gradually discover that challenges which initially seem impossible become manageable through repetition and experience. That sense of growth forms one of the game's most satisfying qualities.

Boss encounters add additional variety by introducing larger challenges built around unique attack patterns and survival demands. These moments often become highlights because they require players to combine everything learned throughout earlier levels. Fast reactions, positioning awareness, and movement precision all become equally important during these encounters. Defeating major obstacles creates a satisfying payoff that reinforces continued progression.

Multiplayer becomes another major strength. Flat Heroes supports cooperative gameplay for up to four players, transforming already intense scenarios into energetic team experiences. Cooperative play introduces additional unpredictability while encouraging communication and coordination. The difficulty remains meaningful even with multiple players involved, creating moments where teamwork becomes just as valuable as individual skill.

Playing cooperatively also introduces a different type of enjoyment compared to solo progression. Group sessions create chaotic but entertaining situations where players work together through increasingly dangerous environments. The cooperative design feels thoughtfully implemented rather than functioning as a simple addition to the main experience.

Competitive options further strengthen replay value by allowing players to challenge one another directly. Combined with challenge modes, score chasing, and additional objectives, the game provides reasons to continue playing long after initial completion. The design consistently encourages improvement and experimentation without relying on artificial progression systems.

Visually, Flat Heroes embraces minimalism with confidence. The geometric presentation remains clean and readable even during intense sequences filled with hazards and movement demands. Bright visual effects and simple animations create personality without overwhelming the screen. The visual restraint works heavily in the game's favor because readability becomes critically important once difficulty increases.

Audio design supports gameplay effectively as well. Sound effects provide useful feedback while music complements both calmer moments and more demanding sequences. The audio presentation strengthens tension without becoming distracting, helping maintain momentum during extended sessions.

The focused nature of Flat Heroes may naturally limit appeal for certain audiences. Players seeking heavy storytelling elements or progression systems built around customization may find the experience narrower in scope than larger platforming adventures. The increasing difficulty can also become intimidating, particularly for players unfamiliar with precision-focused games.

However, those qualities ultimately define what makes Flat Heroes successful. Parallel Circles commits fully to movement-focused gameplay and mechanical refinement rather than chasing unnecessary complexity. Every system reinforces the central goal of creating satisfying platforming built around skill development and precision.

What makes Flat Heroes memorable is how effectively it transforms simplicity into depth. The minimalist appearance hides a remarkably polished experience filled with rewarding challenges and exceptional gameplay flow. It proves that strong mechanics and thoughtful design can create engagement without relying on excessive features.

Players who appreciate challenging platformers, responsive controls, and games centered around mastery will find an experience that consistently rewards effort and improvement. Whether played alone or with friends, Flat Heroes delivers a focused and highly satisfying platforming experience.

An outstanding precision platformer that combines exceptional movement design, rewarding challenge progression, and excellent cooperative gameplay into one of the genre’s strongest minimalist experiences.

5.5小时单人通关普通难度。[h2]上乘之作。 [/h2] 

游戏的优点很多。配色好看，画面简洁，操作优雅，音效上头。用较多的图形而非文字来引导玩家，用还算循序渐进的关卡实现了合格的IPMT，系统简单而有深度，在我这里可以打8.5/10。推荐喜欢挑战自己的玩家（最好有同样喜欢挑战自己的朋友）来游玩。我最早是在和朋友玩switch的时候接触到这款游戏的，一起闯关相当开心。但不得不说在pc上体验更佳。

但是缺点也不得不提，有几个点让我非常恼火（虽然它们并不影响我对这款游戏的喜爱，但我一定要提）。

一、游戏初期掌握弹刀就可以让难度大幅下降，这本来是件好事，因为我是弹刀大师。但是弹刀的范围略小于其视觉表现的范围，在游戏后期对战箭头蛇尤为明显。其行为和吃豆人里的幽灵一样，会兵分多路追围堵截，并且会随机扭动，让弹刀严重失效，让我很不爽。[spoiler] 后来我学会了冲刺弹刀，绕圈打很好用 [/spoiler] 

二、游戏后期敌人引入大量随机行为，使得过关难易度和熟练度非线性相关，极大增加挫败感。点名第八章boss。并且后期相当一部分关卡就是堆砌敌人，没有目的地在空中腾挪，缺乏关卡设计感和明确固定解，约等于碰运气。这种时候就可以感觉到是在”挑战自我“，也就是给自己找罪受，而非在制作者的引导下愉快游戏。

三、令人又爱又恨的跳跃系统。本作角色可以进行一次跳跃和一次空中冲刺，冲刺在弹刀成功/碰到地面或粒子后可以重新充能。平台跳跃游戏中有个可以算跳跃宽容度的变量，大概是指角色在离开地面多少时间后仍可以进行跳跃。而本作作为难度较高的平台跳跃游戏，该宽容度相对来说太高了，很多时候明明已经离开了平台，在想要向下冲刺规避敌人的时候反而会进行一次毫无机动性的向上的初始跳跃，让人极为恼火。并且初始跳跃和冲刺之间存在一个较长的cd，以及在两个表面之间反复横跳时很容易按不出想要的冲刺而是被新的初始跳跃替代，这些特性都极大影响了角色的机动性。

四、竞赛模式中，在占点模式里使用小型地图还算不错，但是其他几个模式，尤其是夺旗模式严重感到地图狭小，游戏混乱。且重生自带的无敌在小图里面非常op，单挑的时候需要注意。

五、前面还说IPMT做得好，但是最后一关的BOSS战居然给出了从来没有见过的机制，追逐模式里面倒是也用到了，可是出现得未免也太突兀了。用摇杆控制射击方向，且该方向与人物移动方向共用，体验不算很好。

六、结合极简画风和配置寥寥的菜单，有时可以感受到制作者的一种傲慢——虽说这未必是坏事，就像早期的ios一样；但是当卡关时，尤其是前面所述的堆砌敌人的关卡时，真的让人只会无能狂怒。制作者也确实一点没考虑键鼠潜在的操作优势，甚至不给一个改键位的选项。

总的来说瑕不掩瑜，大家可以趁打折赶紧入手。我就是因为急着通关才发现这么多问题的，足见其上头程度。

[h1]————————————[/h1]
[h1]重生之我在平面世界当英雄[/h1]
简介
平面英雄是款极简的平台跳跃游戏，正如其名你将在一个2D平面内扮演一个正方体英雄，化解一波波由线条和形状抽象而来的怪物的袭击。
返璞归真的游戏玩法
本作最多可支持本地四人同屏游玩，拥有竞赛、生存、对抗三种游戏模式。奈何拥有此游戏的steam好友较少，因此只侧重说说单人游玩的竞赛模式。竞赛模式共有10个大关（世界），每个世界中又有十来个小关。游戏节奏十分紧凑，在一个有限的平面内存活到最后或消灭所有敌人即可通关，其中一个小关卡短至数十秒即可通关，最长也不会超过几分钟。身为堂堂平面英雄，却只有移动、跳跃、防御三大基础能力，英雄虽没有锋利的宝剑，但是有矫健的身姿，翻滚、闪避、二段跳（维吉尔哭晕在厕所，连方块都会二段跳233），旋转跳跃，在枪林弹雨中片叶不沾身。密集的陷阱与敌人攻击下，返璞归真的操作方式亦能让人肾上腺激素飙升，利用防御撞击敌人也颇有只狼中打铁的韵味，屡试不爽。随着游戏的不断深入，玩家熟练度上升，游戏又将引入新机制与全新的敌人，以适应玩家不断提高的兴奋阈值。
化繁为简的艺术风格
游戏的UI极简无比，几个方块几个字便是全部。游戏画面亦是如此，寥寥几笔线条构成场景，简单的点线面构成敌人，最后赋以不同的颜色。巧妙的是，无需任何引导与教程，只需凭借简单的画面与颜色就能上手。玩家只需要添加自己的想象力让这个世界更加生动：密密麻麻的折线是能量极高的激光，发射三角形攻击的六边形是火力密集的炮塔，蓝色的箭头是骇人的追踪导弹……由你操作的方块主角就像007中的主角邦德总能在一次次危机中化险为夷。
总结
本作难度适中，且游戏流程短平快，非常适合在碎片化时间游玩。在网游漫长的匹配阶段来上一把热热手，岂不美哉。推荐感兴趣的朋友在骨折的时候购入。

Hate to give this one a negative review, especially because it has a slick interface, a fun design, and interesting boss levels. But the game does two things that drag the experience into frustratingly unplayable for single player, and dubious in coop.

First, there's very little texturing for folks that are colorblind. You can lock colors (which helps), but especially on smaller screens like the Steam Deck, color hints and visual cues are somewhat difficult to see. It's frustrating, but on its own, not a dealbreaker.

The much bigger problem is the lack of precision of the game's hitboxes and controls. There's a noticeable latency between when I hit a button and when my character moves. On its own this also isn't a dealbreaker. But when you combine that with how parries work (which become required later) and having the entire rotating box model as a hitbox, it makes for many, many, many unfair and frustrating deaths.

See, one of the secrets of bullet-hell-style games is having a consistent (typically pixel-sized) hitbox at the center of the player model. This means that if flashy animated sprites get clipped by the edge of an attack, it doesn't result in a surprising (and typically unavoidable) death.

Here, not only do these annoying deaths happen often, but they combine with both the input latency and dodgy parry tracking to result in very common deaths from mechanics you intended to parry or dodge. While the levels are pretty well-designed and the bosses have interesting mechanics, interacting with them gets more frustrating the more complicated their attack patterns get, especially when directional parrying objects becomes required.

Cooperative play does smooth over many of these problems by giving the player more meat for the metaphorical grinder, but honestly, this could have been fixed with more playtesting and a tighter control scheme. I had a lot of fun early on, but by the later worlds felt frustrated and annoyed as the control jank sapped any fun I was having.

For a game that does it well, consider Just Shapes & Beats instead. It has tighter controls, better hitboxing, and fun levels and beats besides. This one can be fun if you have a crowd comfortable with its moderate-but-significant control jank, but for my piece, I'd prefer sending up a flare to the developers to tighten it up first.

ワールド1からワールド10まであり、
1ワールド15ステージという構成で
15ステージ目はボスがいる。

ゲームルールはシンプルでステージ毎に設定された
弾幕をすべて回避すればクリア。
ミスすればそのステージの最初からやり直し。

操作はアナログスティックで移動となり、方向キーは非対応。
ジャンプボタンでジャンプし、ジャンプ中にもう一度押すと
任意の方向に素早く移動するエアダッシュが使える。

途中からは攻撃もできるようになり、それはジャンプとは
別のボタンが割り当てられる仕様だ。

ちなみにこれら基本ルールや操作説明はゲーム内で
説明が一切ない。

文字を排したパズルは文字無しでもルールが分かるような
スマートな作品も多いが本作はその対極に当たる。
説明が必要なゲームなのに説明がないとか笑わせる。

プレイ時間としては1ワールド15分～20分ほどでクリアできるが
難易度は高めで死んでは繰り返す心の折れない精神力が必要になる。

ただ本作は「難しいのに眠い」のが問題だ。
精密操作が必要でノーミスでのクリアが前提なので
刺激的なはずだが不思議と眠くなる。

なぜかといえば「ミスしたら最初から」が原因と考える。

プレイを続けていると1ステージが長くなっていくのだが、
これがダメな感じに足を引っ張っている。
ミスしたら最初からやり直しのせいで前回ミスした地点までは
同じ動きで対応できる局面が多いため、
ミスをすればするほどそこへ到達するまでの過程が
ただのルーチンワークとなるからだ。
それが面白いであろうはずがない。

極めつけがボス。
こちらから攻撃して倒すことになるのだが、
攻撃できる機会が限られ、そのチャンスが来るまでは
ひたすら回避に専念するしかないのでひどく地味なのだ。

しかもランダム性ではなく、完全にパターンの攻撃は
毎回同じように回避するだけなのでボス戦の後半でミスると
精神的にやり直しがきつくなってくる。
なおボスステージは通常ステージの数倍長い。

ゲームデザインについてもワールド1～3まではワールド単位での
大きな変化が感じられたがワールド4からは
不毛な覚えゲーと感じるようなパターンゲーと化していったのが
プレイをやめるトドメとなった。

敵の攻撃を見ながらうまい具合に立ち回るのが
ワールド3までの楽しみ方だったのだが、
ワールド4になると立ち回りどうこうというより
避ける場所が決まっているところが多いので、
何回も死んで安全地帯を探すだけの
別ゲーへと変化してしまっていた。
（ワールド1～3までも覚えゲー部分はあったが
　ワールド4ほど露骨な多さではなかった）

面白ければ良かったがこれが面白くないのだから
プレイヤーとしてはひたすらつらい。

シビアなバランスはけっこうなんだが、
本作の場合それが面白さに繋がっていないのが致命傷。

ちなみにワールド4クリアの実績取得率は20%を切っている。
難しすぎたのか面白くなかったのか
どちらが原因でやめたのか興味深いところ。

なお、本作はRemort play together対応のタイトルだが、
これを他の人と遊ぼうという気にはなれない。
（そもそもシビアなゲームはRemort play togetherで
　一緒に遊ぶ上で受けは悪い）

I started playing this game around when it first came out on switch, and even though I stopped for a while after moving to PC, it's some of the most fun I've had with friends in a co-op game. Also this game doesn't have many reviews on Steam, so I'm gonna say it's criminally underrated.

Pros:
The soundtrack is really good
The enemies have a good amount of variety (which is surprising considering that they don't have too many shapes to work with)
The movement is pretty neat in theory (I'll get to that in the cons section)
There are a lot of weird/cool interactions that different enemies and player abilities have, and discovering them is pretty fun
There are a lot of levels and different survival/versus modes, and they really aren't as repetitive as people say
The bosses are (mostly) epic, especially World 2 on Heroes difficulty

Cons:
There are some big difficulty spikes once you get to Heroes difficulty in the campaign
Your movement abilities aren't very consistent, so it's difficult to tell how many dashes you can get out of one multi-dash, or if you'll even get one at all, and how colliding with enemies impacts that
There is a somewhat steep learning curve, although the game does a good job of easing you into different mechanics
Survival and campaign are both considerably easier in co-op, but the game is still entirely possible in single player. Don't let it get you down
Some bosses aren't epic

TLDR the game is really cool except when it's not but those parts are few and far between so play it because it's really underrated

Despite my positive recommendation, I have one major complaint about this game: your avatar is a square that rolls to move.

Hrm... a SQUARE that ROLLS... does anyone else see the problem with the physics of this?

So if you want to move your square just a little bit, you are out of luck because the square will roll back to where you started or will roll further forward than you want if you hit a certain threshold.  If your square is tilted in air, you could land on your corner and move into danger.  If you land on the edge of a ledge, even if you are flat, if your center of mass is not on the ledge, you can roll off.  You can wall cling, but only if one of the sides of your square completely touches the wall, so again, if your square is tilted and you hit the wall with a corner, this can mess you up.  I can’t tell you how many times I got fracked by this baffling mechanic.  In my humble opinion, it doesn’t make the game any more fun or unique, the game is way too hard otherwise to warrant this extra challenge, and it actually goes against the game’s minimalist street cred (if it were me, I would have made it more like Thomas Was Alone and have the little squares just slide along instead).

Other than this, the game is pretty fun.  I do like the soundtrack, level design, basic premise, and various color palates.  The game can be glitchy at times, but that might be my subpar hardware.  And I have to admit that getting all of the achievements in single-player mode was really satisfying (which is what ultimately tipped me in the direction of a thumbs-up), but I just had to vent about those goram rolling squares...
